result.rationale: The webhook handler in apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts uses prisma.credential.findFirst followed by separate create/update with no transaction or unique-constraint handling, exactly as the finding describes. Two concurrent requests can both pass the findFirst null check and both call create, producing duplicate (userId, appId) credentials; subsequent updates then target only the arbitrary first match while the other drifts. The mechanism is fully visible in the diff and is a genuine correctness/data-consistency defect.

judged_text: The webhook deduplicates with findFirst-then-create and no unique constraint on (userId, appId) backs the check. Two concurrent deliveries for the same user and app (a bulk push when the feature is switched on) both find no row and both insert, leaving duplicate credentials; every later webhook updates an arbitrary one of the duplicates via findFirst while the other drifts stale, and type-based credential resolution operates on both.

adjudication.rationale: In the new webhook handler (`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`), credential persistence is implemented as `findFirst` (by `userId` + `appId`) followed by either `update` or `create`. This read-then-write sequence is not atomic and is vulnerable to concurrent requests: two deliveries for the same `(userId, appId)` can both observe “no credential” and both proceed to `prisma.credential.create(...)`. Subsequent webhook calls again use `findFirst` and will update an arbitrary matching row, leaving other duplicates stale. The diff does not show any transaction/locking or `upsert`/unique-constraint-based enforcement to prevent this race.
